April 2010 ## Recovery gaining momentum - Global consumption of copper and copper alloy mill products reached 2.3Mt in the first quarter of 2010, compared to 1.8Mt for the same period in 2009. Our data suggests that flat rolled products and alloy rod demand have certainly improved from Q4 2009, but we still question whether the trend is sustainable in some regions. Battered by the construction sector, copper tube demand is still below the already weak level of Q1 2009. - We believe that world demand is firming up and semis fabricators consequently now hold a relatively more optimistic view compared to the previous quarter. On a regional basis, Asia is still leading the global recovery, with consumption amounting to 1.4Mt in Q1 with volumes in all product segments having returned to pre-crisis levels. We believe that North America as a whole has a better short term outlook than Europe but the US commercial construction sector is still deteriorating. 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 12 **April 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Plate, sheet, strip and foil Our data shows that global copper and copper alloy flat rolled product output increased y-o-y in the first quarter of 2010 by 36% and 46% respectively, supported by production in North East Asia and Developing Asia. One should note that such strong growth partly reflects y-o-y comparisons with the lowest point of the market in Q1 2009 instead of significant sequential growth. On one hand, we continue to see new capacity coming on stream in China and that domestic demand is so strong that it is also underpinning exports from nearby countries. In the Western World, both the Americas and Europe are experiencing a mild recovery in their copper alloy plate, sheet, strip and foil markets, which feed into production of auto parts, coinage and ammunition, but copper flat rolled product markets in both regions are still lagging behind Asia. ### German market outperformed others in Europe European consumption of copper and copper alloy flat rolled products totalled 165,000t in the first quarter of 2010, compared to 143,000t for the same period in 2009. This result is driven by a 29% y-o-y upturn in alloy plate, sheet, strip and foil consumption, which accounted for 77,000t in the European flat rolled market in Q1 2010. The German market experienced an increase in flat rolled consumption for the first quarter, with copper products growing by 30% y-o-y and alloy products growing by 35% y-o-y. Italian manufacturer **KME** said that it is expecting a 12% recovery in its production volume for the first quarter of 2010. It said that copper demand in Europe will be led by auto, white goods and mechanical appliances sectors. The company has seen strong recovery signs in Germany, while Spain and Portugal remains the weakest links. Our data suggests that Spanish production volumes are well below year-ago levels and the trend is likely to continue until any improvement is seen in the construction sector. As confirmed by another major European fabricator, German producers have managed to increase both domestic and export market shares. Underlying demand in Northern Europe is healthy and the automotive sector is restocking. Nevertheless, fabricators remain bearish on demand from Eastern and Central Europe. We estimate that the region produced 60,000t of copper and copper alloy flat rolled product

s in the first quarter, compared to 46,000t in the same period in 2009. ### Chinese consumption supported by on-going schemes Asian flat rolled products consumption is estimated to have been 682,000t in the first quarter of 2010, compared to 449,000t in the same period of 2009. The increase is mainly attributed to sustainable market growth in China and a strong rebound in North East Asia. Japanese copper products output totalled 67,000t in the first quarter of 2010, an increase of 67% y-o-y. **Mitsubishi Shindoh** is planning to expand production of copper strip at the Sambo plant and Wakamatsu plant for exports. South Korean copper products production saw an increase of 83% y-o-y for the same period. Chinese production of copper and copper alloy flat rolled products totalled 336,000t in the first quarter of 2010, compared to 241,000t in Q1 2009. We understand that the home appliance and automotive subsidy schemes have been carried forward from last year, which will continue to support domestic demand. Market growth will be supported by demand for household appliance and infrastructure markets, according to market participants. The Electric Copper Branch of China Electronics Materials Industry Association also reported that copper foil demand is expected to increase to 199,000t in 2010, compared to 185,000t in 2009, and forecasts copper foil demand to reach 218,000t in 2011 and 232,000t in 2012. Encouraged by robust consumption, companies are ramping up new capacity in China. **Hefei Tongguan Guoxuan Copper Semis Co Ltd** went into trial production of its 5,000t/y copper foil project in February 2010 while **Changxing Copper** has commissioned a new 25,000t copper flat rolled product project in April 2010. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 **April 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products **www.crumonitor.com** |Copperpla|te,s|heet|,stri|pand|foil|||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|||**2008**|||**% Ch**|||**2009**|||**% Ch**|**2010**|**% Ch**| ||**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**

We have revised up our output number for Q4 2009 to 500,000t; the figure was up by 1% y-o-y but down by 10% sequentially. The largest national contributor was China, which produced 39% of the world total in Q1. The US fabricated 59,000t in Q1, down by 19% y-o-y and up by 1% q-o-q. Production levels in Q4 2009 contracted by 27% compared with Q4 2007, when US copper tube output amounted to 81,000t. World consumption is estimated to have totalled 523,000t in Q1 2010, with China leading the way as in production at 177,000t. The vulnerable copper tube product segment continued to remain under strong copper substitution pressures. With copper prices close to US$8,000/t in early / mid-April and an average copper to aluminium price ratio of 3.3 in the first quarter of the year, substitution threats from aluminium, plastics and composite materials remain persistently strong. This is having a more significant impact compared to earlier copper price rallies due to tightened liquidity, increased competition and lower profit margins caused by the global economic crisis in 2008-2009. ### Copper tube trade highlights According to our estimates, Chinese exports of copper tube amounted to 35,000t in Q1 2010. The figure accounted for 28% of world exports compared with 27% in the same period of 2009, and partly justifies the long-term capacity growth in China. German copper tube exports reached an estimated 17,100t in Q1 2010, a 13% decline from the same period in 2009. The long-term decline in German exports is primarily associated with customer migration and a depressed construction sector in Europe. Greek exports are estimated to have grown by 22% y-o-y to an estimated 10,900t in Q1 2010. In addition, our figures show that Italian exports of copper tube declined by 18% y-o-y to an estimated 7,400t in Q1 2010. Compared with our earlier estimates in February, we have revised up the Q4 2009 export figures for the UK, Greece, Finland, the Czech Republic and Australasia. We have also revised up our Q4 2009 import numbers for Italy, Spain, the UK, Finland, Netherland, and South Africa. The

US is estimated to have been the world’s largest copper tube importer with 21,700t in Q1 2010. However, imports were down by 6% y-oy, following a long-term decline attributed to customer migration to industrialising regions and a troubled construction sector. US imports represented an estimated 20% of global imports in Q1 2010. ### Copper seamless tube decisions still pending in the US The case of US copper tube imports from China and Mexico is still under investigation by the Department of Commerce. As industry contacts told CRU in February, the preliminary determinations into the antidumping issue in the US copper commercial tube market have indeed been postponed until 5th May to allow for adequate time for a thorough investigation. The final determinations are due 75 days after the date of the preliminary investigations. ### Better outlook for the US and Asian markets Some market participants anticipate that North America and Asia will perform better than Europe in tube demand. **Luvata** said that it expects global demand to rebound 10% in 2010, with the US and Asia being the largest drivers as they account for 45% and 30%, respectively, of Luvata’s sales. We estimate that the two regions jointly produced more than 72% of world production in Q1 this year. Tube 2010 is taking place in Dusseldorf, and CRU will visit the trade show to meet with producers and gain first-hand information about new trends, technologies and materials. We will also be discussing with industry participants how this product segment has reacted to the global economic crisis and what the current challenges are in view of a hesitant and uneven economic recovery. 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 6 of 12 **April 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com |Copper tub|e|||||||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|||**2008**|||**% Ch**|||**2009**|||**% Ch**|**2010**|**% Ch**| ||**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**|**Q4**|**Year**|**07-08**|**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**|**Q4**|**Year**|**08-09**|**Q1**|**09-10**| |**_Production_**||||||||||||||| |Canada|5|4|5|4|**19**|10.0|4|4|4|4|**16**|-13.1|5|20.0| |United States

M A,WB|M S||||||||||| © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 7 of 12 **April 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products **www.crumonitor.com** # Alloy rod, bar and section ### Slow progress The global market for alloy rods, bars and sections continues to make a slow recovery during the first few months of 2010. CRU estimates that Q1 volumes were 11% above the seasonally slow fourth quarter of 2009 and registered a sizeable y-o-y increase from the exceptionally weak opening quarter of 2009. Regional comparisons are at their most extreme at present. In Europe there are only the faintest glimmers of any improvement relative to Q4 2009. In North American output is finally improving and is likely to rise to its highest level for six quarters in Q1 2010, based on encouraging shipments data for the first two months. However, this will still be some way below the already depressed pre-recession levels. In Asia the recovery is very well advanced with China, South Korea and Taiwan showing startling y-o-y growth from the depths of recession in early-2009. There are even some signs of sequential gains in Japan, although these are relatively modest. ### US awakens from slumber US brass rod and wire production rose to its highest level for fourteen months, reaching 19,720t in January, a 21% y-o-y increase. Output dropped slightly to 19,145t in the shorter shipping month of February, but this was still enough to record a 27% y-o-y rise. CRU expects that March data will confirm that output exceeded the 20,000t level for the first time since October 2008. Most of the increase has been for the domestic market as there has yet been little improvement in exports to nearby Canada and Mexico. The domestic market increase is largely attributable to limited restocking. The concern remains that the early recovery in Asian markets will siphon brass scrap out of the US, just as mill

s are looking to increase their purchases ahead of a nascent recovery in screw machine shops operating utilisation. ### Silent spring greets European mills As Europe entered recession after the US, it is not really too much of a surprise that the recovery is going to take longer to emerge. Anecdotal evidence suggests some small indications of improvement in Northern Europe, where German mills are starting to see some encouraging sequential gains in their order books. However, there is little optimism about a recovery in Southern European markets where the economic fallout from the Greek financial crisis continues to tarnish the industry’s hopes of any limited revival. The recent escalation in copper prices has driven brass turnings higher, however this will do little to please intermediate and end use consumers who would like to be able to offer more competitively priced products to spur customer demand. The incentive to economise and downsize brass use and to substitute brass for competing materials that are cheaper or lighter has accelerated with the onset of recession. Mills know that they will see some permanent losses in some applications, particularly in plumbing, and also that consumers are actively looking to outsource or offshore production to Asia for cost savings. ### Asian recovery gaining momentum The world economic recovery has been overwhelmingly Asian-centric and this is also being reflected in the relative health of the region’s brass rod industry. Brass rod output in South Korea and Taiwan has been bolstered by a near doubling in export demand to China, where a broad based recovery is now strongly established. Although automotive components are a relatively minor end use market for brass rod this is by far the strongest segment at present, as Chinese vehicle output surged by 77% y-o-y in Q1 2010 to 4.6 million units. Monthly brass rod production in Taiwan has recently improved to over 10,000t, thereby completing a full recovery to levels seen before the recession, while South Korean output is now just short of 20,000t/m which would also represent a complete recovery. Japan is the only major Asian producer to still fall some way short of a true recovery, with monthly output of around 17,000t. This is 7,000t more than a year-ago, but well below more normal industry levels of 20,000t/m. 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 12 **April 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com |Copper allo|yro|ds,b|ars a|nd s|ectio|ns||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**

m rates.|909.9|1068.2|_923.4_|_942.5_| 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 10 of 12 **April 2010** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Industry news ### North America - Preliminary determinations of antidumping investigations for imports of seamless refined copper tube from China and Mexico have been postponed to 5th May 2010. The decision followed a request of **Cerro Flow Products** , **KobeWieland Copper Products** , **Mueller Copper Tube Products** and **Mueller Copper Tube Company** for a postponement, so that the **Department of Commerce** will have adequate time to conduct a complete investigation. - **Jeffery Burghardt,** VP of North American metal procurement and global utilities of **Luvata Buffalo** , said that even though the amount of copper stored in warehouses has increased substantially since the end of 2008, the copper price has risen more than 100% over the same period. Speaking on behalf of the **Copper and Brass Fabricators Council** , he noted that high copper prices and unprecedented copper price volatility are attributed to investment firms’ large positions in the copper market. However, it was stressed that futures markets are important to copper fabricators as a means of price discovery and price risk management for their day-to-day business. It was suggested that higher margin requirements rather than position limits would discourage speculative trading and serve better the interests of physical participants. - The **Copper and Brass Servicenter Association** said that copper and alloy semis shipments rebounded strongly in February. Copper semis shipments rose by 11.8% y-o-y to 8.8 million pounds whilst brass and other alloy shipments increased by 7.9% y-o-y to 12.2 million pounds. The association reported that total warehouse shipments were up by 9.5% y-o-y in February. - **Wolverine Tube (Canada) Inc.** , which was sold to a group of Canadian private investors in July 2008, has been renamed **Great Lakes Copper Inc.** The company is Canada’s leading fabricator

of copper tube products for the industrial and refrigeration end-use markets. 

- **EcoSea Farming** announced a seminar to promote the benefits of copper use in salmon and fish farming.  The company, strategic partners of which include the **International Copper Association** and **Codelco** , highlighted the economic, environmental and antimicrobial benefits of copper cages. It is expected that EcoSea Farming will start selling these cages in Chile in H1 2010. 

### Europe 

- It has been reported that **KGHM** and **Hutmen** are at the last phase of negotiations of a partnership. The most probable scenario is that the two companies will remain independent entities, as a full scale merger is unlikely. 

- **KME** expects that European copper demand will recover by 10-15% in 2010.  The Italian copper and alloy semis fabricator anticipates that the recovery will be led by the automotive, white goods and mechanical appliances sectors.  Stronger recovery signs are in Germany and northern Europe whilst Spanish and Portuguese markets remain difficult.  KME’s output contracted by 23% to 437,000t in 2009.  It is expected that production will rise by 10-12% in Q1 2010 and 10-15% in full 2010.  Should construction activity experience growth, output may increase by 18% in 2010. 

### North East Asia 

- The **Japan Copper and Brass Association** reported that output of rolled copper products doubled in February 2010 from the same period in 2009.  Attributed to very low figures in 2009, output soared by 95.9% y-o-y to 68,781t on a seasonally adjusted basis in February 2010.  The increase, which the highest growth rate ever recorded, was the fourth straight month of y-o-y growth. However, when compared with February 2008 the figure was still down by 18.9%.  It is expected that year-on-year comparisons will be more representative after April, since output began to show some recovery and stability signs from April 2009. 

- It was reported that **Mitsubishi Shindoh** is increasing capacity of copper alloy strip to meet export demand which it expects will eventually account for 25% of total output.  Currently, capacity amounts to 10,000t/m.  The company’s target is to meet demand in emerging markers.

- The **Japan Copper and Brass Association** expects that demand for rolled copper products, including exports, will increase by 21.4% to 907,430t in FY 2014 from FY 2009.  It is estimated that demand reached a 33-year low of 747,300t in FY 2009.  In addition, it is expected that demand will be 855,490t in FY 2010, 867,150t in FY 2011, 884,330t in FY 2012 and 896,030t in FY 2013. Copper sheet and strip is forecast to grow at a CAGR of 5.1% to 301,000t in FY 2014 from FY 2009, supported by strong demand from the terminal connector and semiconductor lead frame enduse segments.  In the same period, demand for brass bar is a

nticipated to grow at a CAGR of 4.3% to 202,500t on recovering construction activity. The market for brass sheet and strip is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.1% to 136,400t.
